description: We are a team of curious minds passionate about technology, space exploration, artificial intelligence, data science, and innovation. We believe in using creativity and collaboration to transform real-world challenges into meaningful solutions. Through NASA's open data, we aim to explore new possibilities, experiment with innovative ideas, and build projects that can make a positive impact on our planet
summary:
Cipher Space is a browser-based, first-person zero-gravity satellite spacewalk game. Players fly outside a satellite in orbit above Earth and design a space mission by swapping and tuning subsystem modules, either solo or in a 4-player co-op crew joined with a room code. A live mission HUD instantly updates Net Power, Data Rate, Total Mass and Heat Load, and all four must stay within mission limits before the crew verifies and launches.

It addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by letting learners feel trade-offs that static diagrams rarely show: more data needs more bandwidth, which needs more power, which creates more heat, which needs more cooling mass. It runs in a desktop browser with no install. Telemetry comes from our own simulation model, not real mission data.
details:
What it does and how it works

Zero-G Spacewalk is a browser-based, first-person 3D simulation in which players float as an astronaut on a spacewalk (EVA) and repair and reconfigure a modular satellite, SAT-ALPHA 01, in orbit. The satellite has four swappable subsystem slots: Power, Comms, Chassis, and Science. Players fly with 6-degrees-of-freedom zero-g thruster physics, with automatic flight-assist damping so they don’t drift away. They aim a reticle at a component, then hold left-click and drag it in 3D to tilt solar wings or open thermal louvers. Live telemetry for power, heat, bandwidth, and mass shows whether the satellite has reached Mission Equilibrium for the active mission.

Benefits

  • Makes orbital engineering trade-offs (power vs. thermal vs. bandwidth) tangible instead of abstract.
  • Runs instantly in any modern browser from a link, with no installs, accounts, or backend servers.
  • Supports 4-player co-op, so teams learn specialist roles together.

Intended impact

We want to inspire and educate students and space enthusiasts by showing how real satellite design and spacewalk operations work. The co-op roles (Power, Comms, Thermal, Commander) teach the communication and teamwork that real missions depend on.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • Languages: JavaScript, GLSL (custom shaders), HTML5, CSS3
  • 3D engine: Three.js (WebGL) with physically-based rendering, ACES Filmic tone mapping, and shadow mapping
  • Audio: Web Audio API, with all sound synthesized in real time and no audio files
  • Multiplayer: WebRTC DataChannels with Trystero (Nostr signaling), serverless peer-to-peer
  • Input: HTML5 Pointer Lock API
  • Hosting: Static hosting on Vercel
  • Hardware: Any device with a modern browser, a mouse, and a keyboard

How it is creative

  • Everything is procedural. Earth, clouds, atmosphere glow (a Fresnel shader), a 4,000-star starfield, and all audio are generated by code, so there are no 200MB texture downloads.
  • Tactile 3D drag-to-tune controls replace sliders and menus.
  • Diegetic design: a visor-style AR HUD, a radio comms log, and remote astronauts with suits, headlamps, and animated thruster plumes.
  • Serverless multiplayer that works on a plain static host.

Factors our team considered

  • Accessibility and performance: lightweight, link-based, and no install needed.
  • Scientific grounding: equations for power generation, net power, and thermal dissipation drive the simulation.
  • Fair teamwork: role permissions mean only the assigned specialist can modify their own subsystem.
  • Smooth gameplay: 20Hz state sync with interpolation (lerp/slerp) keeps remote astronauts moving smoothly.
